question: ap1
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Hysteresis loop of AP-1 occupancy (magnetism analogy)
ideas.description: Ramp a stimulus (e.g., phorbol ester or growth factor dose) up and then back down, and measure AP-1 genomic occupancy (CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN) and target-gene output at matched doses on each branch. A memory mechanism predicts a hysteresis loop, where the ascending and descending curves diverge at the same stimulus level, while a purely reactive system retraces the same path.

ideas.title: Anamnestic recall test with a degron-based memory eraser (immunological memory analogy)
ideas.description: Prime cells with a stimulus, let them rest, then restimulate, comparing primary and secondary AP-1 target-gene induction kinetics and chromatin opening. Using a dTAG or auxin degron on JUN or FOS applied only during the rest interval, a true memory should be lost (secondary response reverts to primary), separating the role of persistent AP-1 from its acute activity.

ideas.title: Pulse-chase half-life of AP-1 binding (radioactive decay analogy)
ideas.description: Pulse-label endogenous JUN/FOS with a HaloTag or SNAP-tag and track the fraction of tagged protein and of chromatin-bound AP-1 after a stimulus is withdrawn, fitting decay curves at individual enhancers. Comparing the half-life of bound complexes with the half-life of the transcript and protein reveals whether AP-1 occupancy outlasts its trigger on a timescale long enough to count as memory.

ideas.title: Synthetic bistable toggle with an AP-1 feedback loop (electronic flip-flop analogy)
ideas.description: Build a synthetic circuit in which an inducible FOS/JUN cassette drives its own expression through AP-1 sites and reads out a fluorescent reporter, then test whether a brief inducer pulse produces a persistent ON state after the inducer is removed. Varying the strength of the positive feedback and the AP-1 site number maps the conditions required for bistability, which is a necessary property of a memory element.

ideas.title: Lineage recording of past AP-1 activity (cell-tape recorder analogy)
ideas.description: Use an AP-1-responsive promoter to drive a CRISPR-based or base-editing recorder that writes irreversible barcode mutations into a tape locus whenever AP-1 is active. Then track the recorded cells by single-cell lineage and transcriptomics, asking whether cells with a prior AP-1 record show altered responses to a later, unrelated stimulus relative to unrecorded sister cells, which tests whether past AP-1 activity causally shapes future behavior.
